document.title: GTMI Implementation Complexity Tiers Analytical Note
document.data_source: World Bank GovTech Dataset (December 2025 release), GTMI 2022 and 2025 waves

sections.title: Background and motivation
sections.content: The GTMI measures digital transformation across 48 indicators covering CGSI, PSDI, DCEI, and GTEI. This note proposes a five-tier Implementation Complexity Framework classifying each indicator by the type of government action required. The tiers are sequentially ordered, each building on prerequisite capacity of the previous.

tiers.label: Regulatory and Policy
tiers.description: Achieved through legislation, executive orders, or strategy documents. Low financial cost; primary requirement is political will and technical drafting capacity.

tiers.label: Institutional Setup
tiers.description: Creating agencies, authorities, and governance bodies. Requires budget, mandate, leadership, and cross-government coordination.

tiers.label: Frameworks and Standards
tiers.description: Technical architectures, interoperability standards, digital signature regulation. Critical enabler without which systems cannot communicate or be reused.

tiers.label: Government-internal Platforms
tiers.description: Core digital infrastructure primarily used by government officials and agencies.

tiers.label: Citizen- and Business-facing Services
tiers.description: Digital services whose primary interface is to an external party. Requires all Tiers 1-4 as prerequisites.

sections.title: Global adoption trends 2022 to 2025
sections.methodology_note: Adoption = percentage of economies with indicator score > 0. Excluded from trends: I-40, I-41, I-26.
key_findings: Tier 2 strongest global growth (+9.7pp): GovTech entities (I-33: +9pp), data governance bodies (I-34: +12.7pp), innovation programs (I-46: +14.8pp).
Tier 4 flat at 82%. Bimodal: legacy PFM systems at 93-98%, modern infrastructure at 44-68%.
Tier 3 laggard tier, only +2.7pp — structural risk for future T4/T5 investments.
Tier 5 modest growth (+3pp). Open data portals (I-29) apparent -12.8pp. Citizen engagement (I-32) stuck at 31%.
Tier 1 +5pp (excluding artifacts). OSS policy (I-15) only genuine T1 decline (-2pp).

global_tier_adoption_summary.label: Policy
global_tier_adoption_summary.key_observation: Slight gain after excluding methodology artifacts

global_tier_adoption_summary.label: Platforms
global_tier_adoption_summary.key_observation: Flat average masks bimodal: legacy fiscal (93-98%) vs modern (44-68%)

global_tier_adoption_summary.label: Services
global_tier_adoption_summary.key_observation: Modest growth; I-29 declining; I-32 stuck at 31%

regional_tier_change.key_signal: High baseline; T2 surge (data gov entity +18.9pp)
Fastest-growing; unique T3 gain; T4 flat (at ceiling)
Only region with T4 decline; WoG (I-36) -16pp
T1 flat; biggest T2 gain; open gov portal (I-28) +27pp
Largest T2 gain; I-29 -46pp (artifact); T5 weakest globally

regional_findings.summary: Benchmark region (avg GTMI 0.762). Sharpest gains: I-34 +18.9pp, I-46 +13.2pp, I-47 +11.3pp. Legacy T4 systems at ceiling (100%).
Most dynamic region. Only region with strong T3 gains (+9.4pp), WoG I-36 +25pp. Only region where T5 (+7.7pp) rivals T2.
Structural warning: T3 declining (-5pp), enterprise arch (I-2) -14.3pp. Concurrent heavy T2 investment (+10.3pp). Without T3, institutions cannot produce interoperable systems.
Only region with both T3 and T4 declining. I-36 -16.1pp; I-9 and I-10 each -16.1pp. May reflect stricter self-assessment by Gulf states in 2025.
T1 flat (-0.5pp); OSS policy (I-15) -12.1pp. T2 standout (+11.1pp): I-46 +21.2pp, I-33 +15.2pp. Open government portals (I-28) +27.3pp.
Highest T2 growth (+12.2pp): I-33 +14.6pp, I-45 +14.6pp, I-46 +18.8pp. T3 also +8.8pp. T5 weakest globally at 52.6%; I-32 at just 8.3%.

observations.title: The Tier 4 ceiling is not universal
observations.detail: Legacy PFM systems saturated from decades of donor-funded builds. Modern T4 (cloud, service bus, PIMS) has substantial growth potential.

observations.title: Tier 2 institutional investment surging globally
observations.detail: Institutions without T3 frameworks and T4 platforms cannot deliver impact. LCR exemplifies this risk.

observations.title: Tier 3 is the structural bottleneck
observations.detail: Enterprise architecture and interoperability frameworks have weakest growth of any actionable tier. All downstream indicators depend on T3.

observations.title: SAR offers the most integrated reform model
observations.detail: Only region growing meaningfully across T1, T3, and T5 simultaneously, suggesting coordinated reform design.

observations.title: Citizen engagement remains structurally underfunded
observations.detail: I-32 at 31% globally, barely moved from 2022. Governments have built platforms but not used them for accountability.

annexes.title: Methodology and replication notes

data_sources.data_2022: 199 economies via online survey + desk research
data_sources.scope: Top-level indicators I-1 through I-48 only. Sub-indicators excluded.

annexes.tier_averaging: Simple unweighted means of adoption rates within each tier.

excluded_from_trends.reason: Definitional narrowing 2022-2025; not actual policy rollback
2022 reflects broader ICT ethics; 2025 specifically AI ethics for GovTech

replication_steps: Filter to Year==2022 and Year==2025; map Reg column (AFR->SSA)
Identify indicators with regex ^I-\d+$ on df.columns
Group by region; assign to tiers per Annex A
